explanations.answer: The man who fears the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The psalm says, "Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments." Notice who gets the blessing. The psalm names the man who fears the LORD.

explanations.answer: The man who leads an army
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd go there, friend. Armies look impressive from a distance, and I'd probably salute one too. But the psalm never mentions a soldier. It says, "Blessed is the man who fears the LORD…" (Psalm 112:1).

explanations.answer: The man who builds a city
explanations.explanation: A whole city, friend! That's a lot of bricks, and I can barely build a stack of cookie boxes without a lean. But the psalm doesn't bless the builder. It blesses "…the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1).
Yes, friend! The psalm says he "…greatly delights in His commandments." Not puts up with them, not squints at them. He delights. That's the face of someone who loves what he's been given.
I hear you. Plenty of us struggle, and I've fought a rolling pin or two myself. But that's not what this verse says about him. It says he "…greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1).

Hesitating is me at the oven door, friend, wondering if the batch is done. But that's not what this verse says about him. The psalm says he "…greatly delights in His commandments." (Psalm 112:1). That word is delights.
True, friend. The psalm says, "His descendants will be mighty in the land…" The blessing doesn't stop with him. It reaches past him to the ones who come after.

Close, but this one is true, friend. The psalm says, "His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed." That's straight from the verse. The family tree gets the blessing too.
True! The psalm says, "…his righteousness endures forever." Wealth and riches sit in his house, but the righteousness is the part that never runs out. Nobody has to check the pantry for that one.

I can see why you'd doubt it, friend, because most things we make don't last. My cookies last about four minutes. But the psalm says it plainly: "…his righteousness endures forever." (Psalm 112:3). So this one is true.

That's it, friend. The psalm says, "Light dawns in the darkness for the upright…" I know a little about dark places, and when light shows up in one, you never forget it. This light is for the gracious, compassionate and righteous.
A river would be a nice surprise, friend, though I'd worry about my flour. But the psalm talks about something else. It says, "Light dawns in the darkness for the upright…" (Psalm 112:4).

A wall sounds sturdy, friend, and I like sturdy. But that's not what the psalm gives. It says, "Light dawns in the darkness for the upright—for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous." (Psalm 112:4).

explanations.answer: He is generous and lends freely
explanations.explanation: Right on, friend. The psalm says, "It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely, whose affairs are guided by justice." He gives and lends without clutching his purse. And the psalm says it is well with him.

explanations.answer: He spends it all on himself
explanations.explanation: Ha, spending it all on yourself is a tempting plan, friend. But the psalm describes someone else. It says, "It is well with the man who is generous and lends freely…" (Psalm 112:5). His money goes out to others, not just to himself.

explanations.answer: He keeps his money hidden away
explanations.explanation: Under the mattress, friend? I think that's a lonely place for money. The psalm says it is well with the man "…who is generous and lends freely…" (Psalm 112:5). Nothing there about hiding it.

I see why you'd pick that, friend, but the psalm says the opposite. It says, "Surely he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever." Never shaken. That's the real word in the verse, so this one is false.
False is right, friend. The psalm says, "Surely he will never be shaken…" Not shaken now, not shaken later. And it adds that "the righteous man will be remembered forever." (Psalm 112:6).

explanations.answer: His heart trusts in the LORD
explanations.explanation: You got it, friend. The psalm says, "He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD." The psalm doesn't say he knows the news ahead of time. It says his heart is trusting in the LORD.
Good friends are a gift, and I wish mine had been awake more in that drawer. But the psalm doesn't give that as the reason. It says his heart is "…steadfast, trusting in the LORD." (Psalm 112:7).

explanations.answer: His mind knows what is coming
explanations.explanation: I'd love a crystal ball for my oven, friend. But the psalm doesn't say he knows what's coming. It says, "He does not fear bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD." (Psalm 112:7). His trust is what holds him steady.
That's right, friend. The psalm says, "He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor…" Scattered, like seed tossed out by the handful. This man gives his gifts wide.
Priests are a fair guess, friend, since giving and worship often go together. But this verse names someone else. It says, "He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor…" (Psalm 112:9).
Rulers have plenty already, friend, and I don't think they're waiting on my cookies. The psalm says, "He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor…" (Psalm 112:9). His gifts go to those in need.

explanations.answer: He will be grieved and gnash his teeth
explanations.explanation: Yep, friend. The psalm says, "The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away…" It's a heavy ending for him. The psalm closes by saying, "the desires of the wicked will perish."

explanations.answer: He will change his ways and give
explanations.explanation: That would be a happy turn, friend, and I like happy turns. But the psalm doesn't say that. It says the wicked man "…will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away…" (Psalm 112:10).

explanations.answer: He will laugh and walk away
explanations.explanation: A big laugh and a casual stroll, friend? That's not what the psalm shows. It says, "The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away…" (Psalm 112:10). It's a heavy verse, so I'll keep this one simple.
